claims.text: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi or its derivatives exhibit high saturation magnetization and coercive fields at or below approximately 100 Oe.
A brief controlled aging treatment can nucleate a minor volume fraction of nanoscale coherent precipitates in an fcc FeCoNi-based matrix.
The precipitates can consist of a chemically ordered phase with high magnetocrystalline anisotropy, such as an L10-like phase.
A suitable aging window can retain a mostly fcc matrix while producing uniformly dispersed nanoscale secondary-phase precipitates.
Excessive aging can coarsen the precipitates or trigger extensive phase transformation.
Nanoscale secondary-phase precipitates create local regions of enhanced magnetic anisotropy in the fcc matrix.
The anisotropic precipitate regions act as strong domain-wall pinning sites.
Localized variations in magnetocrystalline anisotropy increase the energy barrier for domain-wall motion.
Increasing the energy barrier for domain-wall motion increases the coercive field.
The aged alloy will have a significantly higher room-temperature coercive field than a matched as-solutionized single-phase fcc baseline.
The aged alloy is anticipated to exhibit a coercive field substantially above 100 Oe, potentially at least twice the baseline value.
The coercivity enhancement can occur without a drastic reduction in saturation magnetization.
Full phase transformation or excessive precipitate coarsening might lower saturation magnetization or cause unwanted brittleness.
